tools.name: analyze_sql
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a complete review of a SQL query. Runs validate, parse, metadata, security, lint, and format concurrently and returns one composite report; hosts that support MCP Apps render it as an interactive report.

tools.name: extract_metadata
tools.description: Use this when the user wants the tables, columns, and functions a SQL query references (e.g. for lineage or impact analysis). Returns {tables, columns, functions}.

tools.name: format_sql
tools.description: Use this when the user wants SQL pretty-printed or reformatted: one clause per line, optional upper-case keywords and trailing semicolon. Comments are not kept. Returns {formatted_sql, options}.

tools.name: lint_sql
tools.description: Use this when the user wants SQL style feedback. Applies the same 10 rules as `gosqlx lint`: L001 trailing whitespace, L002 mixed indentation, L003 consecutive blank lines, L004 indentation depth, L005 line length (>100), L006 column alignment, L007 keyword case (upper), L008 comma placement (traili

tools.name: parse_sql
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to know how SQL parses: returns an AST summary with the statement count and the type of each statement.

tools.name: security_scan
tools.description: Use this when the user wants SQL checked for injection patterns: tautologies, UNION attacks, stacked queries, comment bypasses, and more. Returns findings with severity counts.

tools.name: validate_sql
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to know whether a SQL statement is syntactically valid, optionally for a specific dialect. Returns {valid: bool, error?: string, dialect?: string}.
